clue.text: Shellfish picked up for contractor?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for the shellfish is taken by its sound

parts.note: a mussel is an edible bivalve shellfish

explanation.surface: A seafood order is collected on behalf of a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contractor' looks like a builder, but the question mark flags a whimsical sense: something that contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle works by contracting, so it is playfully a thing that contracts.

clue.text: Calm river in China

indicators.note: in places the river's name inside the word for friend

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate
the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: A tranquil stretch of river somewhere in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is rhyming slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to calm or temper; as an adjective it means not extreme.

clue.text: Diminutive figure infiltrating drink? It's deceptive behaviour

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the small person goes within the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A tiny person sneaking into a drink is underhand conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is a British term for framing someone, a deceitful set-up.

clue.text: Electrical gear for broadcast in city

indicators.note: for broadcast means said over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: leads are the cables connecting electrical equipment

explanation.surface: Cabling for a radio broadcast in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is an English city, an example of the category.

clue.text: A supporter's not recorded emitting line that's hurtful

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment; with the 's it gives the plural form

indicators.note: emitting means letting out, so the letter for line leaves the word

parts.note: a broadcast not recorded is live

explanation.surface: A fan's off-the-cuff remark, minus one line, still stings.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive remarks are harsh and grating, hence wounding or hurtful.

clue.text: Two animals appear on piece of footage — papers might go into it?

parts.note: a bull and a dog together
a clip is a short extract of film

explanation.surface: Wildlife footage of two creatures, perhaps filed away with the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong spring clamp that grips a stack of sheets together.

clue.text: Fantastic sundial found in pair of areas, one in Spain

indicators.note: found in places the scrambled letters between the two area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two of them give two As

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A wonderful sundial discovered across two Spanish regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is an autonomous region in southern Spain, so it is one region in that country.

clue.text: Admission by plaintive sort, upset artist, sign of pressure

parts.note: a plaintive person might confess with the words I sob

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A weeping artist confesses, a sign of being under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission by plaintive sort' is what a crybaby might confess: two words, I and SOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Musician in underground site plugging European music principally

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the underground site goes between the other letters
principally points to the leading letter of the word music

parts.note: a mine is a site dug below ground

explanation.surface: A performer playing in a cavern, plugging European music.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminem is the stage name of the American rapper Marshall Mathers.

clue.text: Nonsense from liberal behind rally

indicators.note: behind places the letter for liberal after the word for rally

parts.note: a rally or drive is a campaign of effort

explanation.surface: A political complaint: the Liberals' rally speech was rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly talk, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Old lag, one repeatedly moving plants

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about into a new order
repeatedly means the numeral for one is used twice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old convict keeps shifting potted plants around.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDLAG plus II is rearranged. An old lag is British slang for a veteran prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering plants of the iris family.

clue.text: Dependable way to form idols?

parts.note: read the clue backwards: shaking (rocking) the word solid forms the letters of idols

explanation.surface: A question about the reliable method for making statues.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: ROCK is an anagram signal and SOLID its fodder, which rocked makes IDOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rock-solid is utterly reliable, a synonym for dependable.

clue.text: Place offering spin for change?

parts.note: looks like a political spin doctor's office, but it means a shop where coins buy a washing-machine spin cycle

explanation.surface: A spin doctor's office promising change.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated laundry, where you pay small change to have clothes washed and spun.

clue.text: Pass on slogan for Brexit?

definitions.meaning: to decline or abandon something, as in passing on an offer
the side campaigning to quit the EU in the 2016 UK referendum used this one-word slogan

explanation.surface: Declining the option, with a nod to the 2016 referendum slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is to skip or depart; the 2016 Vote ___ campaign wanted the UK out of the EU.

clue.text: They mark lines showing sense with book

parts.note: touch is one of the five senses
Judges is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Teachers marking lines of text with sensible use of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Touch judges are rugby officials who watch the touchlines.
explanation.definitionFit: These rugby officials patrol the sidelines and flag when the ball goes out, so they mark the lines.

clue.text: Fellow wearing this seen batting — it's ideal for bouncers?

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the scrambled letters are worn around the letter for fellow
batting, as in eyelids fluttering, means these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A cricketer seen batting: big build is ideal for bowling bouncers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting' rearranges THIS SEEN to HETINESS around F. Bouncers here are nightclub doormen, not cricket deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulk and weight are a real asset for a nightclub doorman.

clue.text: Holy man subject to criticism badly in need

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
rapped means sharply rebuked

explanation.surface: A saint reprimanded and left needy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strapped, as in strapped for cash, means badly short of money.

clue.text: Permissive couple of workers rejecting India

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the letter for India is dropped

parts.note: a toiler and an ant are two kinds of worker
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two lax labourers who turn down a posting to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant means allowing behaviour others might forbid, a synonym for permissive.

clue.text: Fact soldier manipulated as revolutionary leader

indicators.note: manipulated means worked over by hand, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Truth twisted by a soldier serving as a rebel chief.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Cuban revolution of 1959 and then ruled Cuba for decades.

clue.text: Inactivity shown by soldiers in busy port

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the rearranged port
busy means bustling with activity, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Idle soldiers lounging in a bustling harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is a state of sluggishness and lethargy.

clue.text: Arab dons number, unisex garment

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so one piece is worn around the other

parts.note: a number is a song in a performance
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab performer puts on a costume for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrap of cloth tied at the waist, worn by both men and women.

clue.text: Approval given by a special number for ruminant

parts.note: OK expresses approval or consent
pi is a famous mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A cow is given a nod and a special number tag.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a cud-chewing African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Scoundrel touching legal document

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
probate is the certificate proving a will

explanation.surface: A villain gets mixed up with a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled rogue, a synonym for scoundrel.

clue.text: Foreign river, ending top in repute

indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter is moved to the top

parts.note: the Douro flows through Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: An overseas river whose source has a good name.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in good odour means being in good repute, which is why the word fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean standing or reputation, as in being in good odour with someone.

clue.text: Suitable jacket for trendy flat say

parts.note: proper means suitable or fitting

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of trendy are used

explanation.surface: Choosing a fitting coat for a fashionable apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the flat as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is one example of real estate, a piece of what is owned.

clue.text: Hotel with a pool designed for excitement

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: designed means planned out, so these letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A hotel's swimming pool built to thrill guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla means fuss, commotion or noisy excitement.

clue.text: Indicate range of tenors?

definitions.meaning: to show a reading, as a dial shows a level
the span of pitches a voice type such as a tenor covers

explanation.surface: Show me how high a group of tenors can sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge can register a value; a singer's vocal span is also called this.

clue.text: Sacred itinerant holding distinction

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the answer sits within these two words

explanation.surface: A wandering holy man with an honour to his name.
explanation.definitionFit: In exam grading a credit is a mark of merit, a level of distinction.
